name: orb_breakout_5s
author: adapted from aggregated_from_x_indian_traders
thesis: Exploiting directional breakouts from the first 15-minute opening range caused by institutional order flow imbalance post-auction. Inefficiency exists due to market microstructure (pre-open auction hides true demand until regular session starts) and retail hesitation. Hasn't been arbitraged away because false breaks are frequent in high VIX India, strict volume + index filters + 1-min execution costs eliminate edge for manual traders.
mechanism: The opening range concentrates pending orders and stop-losses on both sides. When price breaches the range boundary, stop-loss orders from wrong-side participants cascade, amplifying the move. Breakout-following algorithms detect the breach and add momentum, creating a self-reinforcing move that typically persists for 60-180 seconds before the order book absorbs the flow.

indicators.name: orb_high_15
indicators.formula: max(high over first 180 bars of day)

indicators.name: orb_low_15
indicators.formula: min(low over first 180 bars of day)

weaknesses: Regime dependency: fails completely in high VIX (>25) choppy days with repeated false breaks
Liquidity constraints: slippage >10 bps on mid-cap FnO names during low-volume breaks
Crowding / alpha decay: ORB widely taught on X and YouTube leading to faster failure in popular stocks
prior_art: Classic Opening Range Breakout (inspired by EQUITIGER algo and common X threads)
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
